guide.summary: GitLab documents OAuth 2.0 for third-party apps to access resources for a user on GitLab.com and self-managed instances. Register an app that requests only read_api, complete authorization with a test account, then test a read of issues through the REST API. Confirm project scope and pagination during that test. Provider review and customer-admin approval are not covered by the supplied sources.

findings.detail: GitLab's OAuth 2.0 identity provider API lets third-party services access GitLab resources for a user. It applies to GitLab.com and self-managed instances.

findings.title: Request read_api for read access
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API and is sufficient for queries. Use it as the requested scope for reading issue titles.

evidence.quote: Scope Access read_api Grants read access to the API. Sufficient for queries.

findings.title: Avoid the write-capable api scope
findings.detail: The api scope grants read and write access and is required for mutations. It is not needed for this read-only use case.

steps.title: Read issue titles from a project
steps.detail: Call the project issues list endpoint with the project ID or URL-encoded path as id. Use a read-only GET request. Each returned issue includes a title; read it from each array item. Responses return 20 results by default. For the next page, use the cursor parameter with the supplied cursor value. Representative input: an accessible project with state=opened. Expected result: a JSON array of issues, each with a title. Boundary check: request an inaccessible or missing project; expect 404 with no issue data. Only GET is used, so no issues are created, updated or deleted.
steps.doneWhen: A GET request to the project issues endpoint returns a JSON array whose items each include a title, and the next page can be retrieved with the cursor parameter. The boundary check returns 404 for an inaccessible or missing project, and no write request is made.

cursor string No Parameter used in keyset pagination.
Responses in this API are paginated and return 20 results by default.

steps.detail: Call the token info endpoint with the token and confirm the granted scope is read_api only. Boundary check: this is a nonmutating GET; confirm no api scope appears.
steps.doneWhen: The token info response lists read_api and does not list api.
